results.ask: I want to do a bonfire at the beach Saturday
results.expect: includes plover season status and fire rules with sources, unprompted; cites
results.answer:
Bonfires at Ocean Beach are allowed only in the provided fire rings between Stairwells 15 and 20, and not at all during the winter no-burn season (November 1 through February 28) to avoid Spare the Air. Since today is November 14, 2026, you're currently in the no-burn season, so bonfires aren't permitted right now.

The NPS manages these rules and posts live alerts about whether the no-burn season is active. You can check the current status on [outersunset.today](https://outersunset.today) or visit the [NPS Ocean Beach page](https://www.nps.gov/goga/learn/management/fire_beachfireregs.htm).

If you plan to return next year (after February 28), remember:
- Use only the designated fire rings between Stairwells 15–20
- Keep fires small and fully extinguished before leaving
- No glass containers near the fire
- Dogs must be leashed (especially important during plover season, July–May 15)

Would you like help finding other beach activities that are allowed during the no-burn season?

results.ask: What's special about my block? I'm on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega.
results.expect: calls about_block; gives the block's own figures and something pinned nearby, with sources; cites
results.answer:
Your block on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega sits about 39 feet above sea level, just 0.2 miles from Ocean Beach, with homes mostly built around 1941 (though the oldest on city records dates to 1908).  

Nearby history includes Doelger’s Rainbow House and Freedom House, built in 1941–42 just a few blocks east, named for wartime hope before construction halted. The Noriega seawall, started in the 1980s, still battles annual sand drifts from the beach—Public Works moved 30,000 cubic yards there in June 2023.  

Old photos are pinned near your corner at 46th & Moraga and a bit southeast at 45th & Noriega in the OpenSFHistory archive.  

The wider stretch shares that every block here rests on dune sand, and the 1906 earthquake began just over two miles offshore.  

Street cleaning: east side Mondays (1st & 3rd), west side Thursdays (1st, 3rd, 5th), noon to 2pm. Signs on the block are final.  

Want to know more? A neighbor who’s lived here since the 1970s could share memories—ask the stewards to pass it along.

results.ask: When is street cleaning on 46th between Moraga and Noriega?

results.answer:
Street cleaning on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega runs as follows, per the city's schedule:

- **East side**: Monday 1st and 3rd of each month, noon to 2pm (next: November 16)
- **West side**: Thursday 1st, 3rd, and 5th of each month, noon to 2pm (next: November 19)

These dates don't apply on city holidays. The signs posted on the block are the final word—they can change, so check them before parking.

results.ask: Any old photos of 46th and Moraga?
results.expect: calls about_block; links the archive's pages and credits them; does not describe pictures it hasn't seen; cites
results.answer:
Yes, there are two old photographs pinned right at the corner of 46th and Moraga in the OpenSFHistory archive, maintained by the Western Neighborhoods Project. You can view them here: [OpenSFHistory / wnp58.929](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.929.jpg) and [OpenSFHistory / wnp58.923](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.923.jpg). Each link opens the image along with its date and caption.

Nearby on the same block, there's also history of the Barefoot Club's streetcar clubhouse from the 1890s-1910s, located about 700 feet north at 46th and Lawton. Back then, many horsecars and cable cars hauled out to the dunes for use as clubhouses—this was near the inland edge of the streetcar settlement which stretched from Lincoln Way south to Moraga Street.

If you want more about what used to be at this corner or how the block has changed over time, a neighbor who knows more about local history could share their memories.
